newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Banks mull 183.1 bln won in emergency loans to Kia.
newsitem.headline: Banks mull 183.1 bln won in emergency loans to Kia.

text.p: Creditor banks of South Korea's troubled Kia Group on Wednesday discussed a Korea First Bank proposal to extend 183.1 billion won in emergency loans to four Kia affiliates, a bank official said.
An official at the Korea First Bank, the biggest commercial bank among Kia's creditors, said the amount compared to 515.9 billion won that the group had earlier requested.
"The meeting is still under way and the exact amount of loans will be decided later," the official said.

The total breaks down into (in billion won, requested amount in brackets): 60.7 (175.0) for Kia Motors Corp ; 76.6 (131.7) for Asia Motors Corp ; 25.0 (140.6) for Kia Steel Co ; and 20.8 (68.6) for Kisan Co.
Creditor banks selected 18 Kia affiliates for bail-out earlier this month after determining that the group would be unable to avoid defaulting on debt payments.
